- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 79.16 or 79.68), then corrects with a downward bias.
- Underestimates in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30) — model lags behind true price movements.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to historical mean faster than actual market behavior.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the 30-day window, suggesting model lacks downward pressure or policy-induced correction logic.
- Model fails to capture sudden policy or supply shocks — true outcomes often spike higher than forecast, especially after 78.00+ in history.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggests model lacks asymmetric volatility modeling.
